state.case_summary:
A man in his 70s presented to the emergency department with progressive dyspnea on exertion. His medical history includes multiple prior cardiac events and lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium. Ten months prior, he had received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery. At presentation, the patient denied chest pain.

No detailed physical examination findings were provided in the case report.

- Laboratory tests: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T (hs-cTnT) level was 40 ng/L (reference range, 0-14 ng/L), unchanged from baseline value obtained 1 month prior.- ECG findings:   - Normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute  - 1.0-mm ST elevation in lead V1  - 4.0-mm ST elevation in leads V2 and V3   - T-wave inversions in leads I, aVL, V4, V5, and V6  - Diffusely low voltages in both limb leads and precordial leads  - Imaging studies:  1. Transthoracic echocardiogram:     Image Title: Apical 4-chamber view     Image Description: Well-circumscribed 2.8 × 2.6-cm mass located in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum     Additional findings:      - Preserved left ventricular systolic function     - No regional wall motion abnormalities     - Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade  2. Coronary angiography:     Findings: Nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease without evidence of acute thrombotic or embolic occlusion
